sentences.text: Pre-operative multi-sequence MRI: axial T1, contrast-enhanced T1 (T1ce), T2 and FLAIR, co-registered, skull-stripped and resampled to 1 mm isotropic (BraTS preparation).
The tumour contains a necrotic / non-enhancing core (confidence 0.53). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The whole-tumour mass is predominantly left-sided (confidence 1.00).
An enhancing tumour component is present (confidence 1.00).
Whole-tumour burden is assessed as large (volume tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.65). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The enhancing fraction of the whole tumour is mid (ET/WT tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.63). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
Acquisition quality (cjv, efc, snr, sharpness, inu, contrast, entropy) is mildly outside the training cohort range (mean |z| = 0.60); interpret borderline findings with corresponding caution.
T1 and T1ce show a hyperintense lesion with a central hypointense area, consistent with a lesion of the left hemisphere.
The lesion has a well-defined margin on both T1 and T1ce images.
DEFERRED TO RADIOLOGIST: case confidence 0.53 is below the calibrated gate threshold 0.55.
For radiologist confirmation: ncr_present present (p=0.53); laterality left (p=1.00).
